quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: You must use low beams when you are:
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Crosswalks are:

options.text: Always marked with lines on the pavement.
Always marked with vertical lines on the pavement.

questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist with or without pavement markings. You must stop behind the crosswalk to let pedestrians cross.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. Slow down or stop when you see it.

questions.question: What is the main concern with this sign?

options.text: Your headlights may be misaligned because one side of your car is higher.
A tire could be damaged from drifting onto the shoulder.
You could hydroplane if water is on the shoulder.
You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head to look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under any railroad gate or barrier.
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one thing while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Opposing traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move your car into each lane as soon as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: What can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic congestion and should be avoided.

questions.question: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel tightly and take your foot off the gas to let the vehicle slow down. Brake lightly when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until your car has slowed down enough.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway if no sign says otherwise?
questions.explanation: On a rural interstate highway, the maximum speed limit is 75 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow the posted sign.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns drivers that a lane is ending so they can let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are traveling through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: When may you drive on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: Only when an official tells you to do so.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
When the car in front of you is turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when an official tells you to do so.
questions.explanation: You may only drive on the shoulder of a road if an official has directed you to do so.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check that your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces this risk.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: First, check traffic and signal. Then, stop parallel to the car directly in front of your parking space. After that, turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you need more following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. Speeds above 80 mph are often fatal. Faster speeds also increase your stopping distance, so you need more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot stop intoxication if you drink too much.
